title: Onboarding Experiments and Fidelity-Cost Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
This playbook defines an experiment-driven approach for onboarding new developer customers to Redwood Inference with an explicit mapping between fidelity profiles, cost signals, and SLA entitlements. The goal is to minimize developer friction while making unit economics predictable and measurable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Audience
- Product managers and go-to-market leads running onboarding pilots
- Solutions engineers and customer success teams executing migrations
- Platform engineers implementing fidelity policy controls and telemetry

Scope and intent
- Defines a set of onboarding experiment cohorts (A/B/C) tied to fidelity presets and priced trial credits.
- Establishes measurable criteria to graduate customers between fidelity tiers.
- Provides rollout steps, required product hooks, billing implications, and rollback guidance.

Definitions
- Fidelity profile: A named bundle of runtime characteristics (model variant, quantization level, batching limits, streaming vs chunked responses).
- Onboarding credit: Time-limited usage credit applied to a tenant to cover trial costs.
- Entitlement SLA: Explicit latency and availability guarantees associated with a pricing tier.

High-level approach
1) Create 3 onboarding cohorts:
   - Cohort A (Exploratory): High-fidelity default model, minimal batching, extended latency budget (200ms p50 target), 1,000 onboarding credits.
   - Cohort B (Balanced): Mid-fidelity variant (int8 or mixed precision), moderate batching, standard latency budget (120ms p50), 2,500 onboarding credits.
   - Cohort C (Economy): Quantized variant with aggressive batching and prefix-caching, tight cost limits, relaxed p50 latency (220ms), 5,000 onboarding credits to demonstrate cost savings.

2) Instrument: Telemetry hooks for per-request fidelity tags, credit burn-rate, per-route latency distribution, and quality regressions tied to shadow-eval prompt sets.

3) Gate graduation: Customers must meet usage and quality thresholds in their cohort for N days before automatic promotion. Promotion is governed by the Fidelity Promotion Rule (FPR) below.

Fidelity Promotion Rule (FPR)
- Inputs (measured over the last 7 days): 1) Daily active tokens >= 10k, 2) Regression rate against shadow prompts <= 1.2x baseline, 3) Average credit burn per 1k tokens within cohort budget.
- If all inputs satisfied for 7/7 days -> promote to next fidelity tier.
- If regression spikes > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive days -> immediate rollback to prior tier and open a fidelity incident.

Required product hooks (implementation checklist)
- Tenant metadata: onboarding_cohort, onboarding_start, onboarding_credits_remaining (API + Console).
- Runtime: fidelity_tag header on inference requests; ability to map fidelity_tag to model variant and quantization profile.
- Billing: trial credit ledger entries and reporting APIs for credit burn by route/model.
- Observability: dashboard showing cohort distribution, credit velocity, p50/p95 latency, shadow-eval regression trend.
- Admin tooling: manual override for promotion/rollback and audit log with who/when/why.

Experiment matrix (example)
(Represented here as a text table; implement as dashboard table in Console)
| Cohort | Model Variant | Quant | Batch Size | p50 Target | Trial Credits | Expected unit cost delta vs baseline |
| Cohort A | redwood-xl-v2 | fp16 | 1-2 | 200ms | 1k | +45% |
| Cohort B | redwood-xl-v2-mix | int8-mix | 4-8 | 120ms | 2.5k | +5% |
| Cohort C | redwood-xl-quant | int8-q | 16-64 | 220ms | 5k | -60% |

Pricing and packaging implications
- Trial credits should be delivered as non-billable ledger items that expire at onboarding_end + 30 days.
- Credits consumed beyond trial convert to regular billing at the tenant's chosen pricing tier.
- Cohort-specific uplift: if customer is kept at Cohort A after trial, charge a 10% fidelity surcharge to reflect higher unit cost; conversely, Cohort C conversion includes a 5% low-fidelity discount.

Quick decision table
- If customer requires regulated private deployment (VPC / on-prem): default to Cohort B unless explicit cost-savings mandate -> run Cohort C only after security review.
- If the customer reports quality complaints within first 72 hours: escalate to CSM; consider one-time temporary credit and possible immediate promotion to higher fidelity for diagnosis.

PRD requirements (minimal viable set for Q4 onboarding pilots)
- PRD-1: New tenant fields (onboarding_cohort, onboarding_expires_at, onboarding_credits) exposed in Accounts API and Console.
- PRD-2: Fidelity tags in inference API with mapping stored in Variant Catalog.
- PRD-3: Credit burn reporting pipeline with hourly aggregation and tenant-level export.
- PRD-4: Shadow-eval integration that runs 1% of requests through shadow variants and surface regression alerts to the Console.
- PRD-5: Console cohort visualization and manual override controls with audit trail.

Design constraints and non-goals
- We will not perform per-request model switching beyond fidelity_tag during onboarding; staged promotion happens at tenant-level only.
- We will avoid introducing new pricing SKUs during pilot; use credit accounting + simple surcharges/discounts.

Telemetry and SLOs
- Required telemetry spans: fidelity_tag, model_variant, quant_profile, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_latency_ms, shadow_eval_result (pass/fail), credit_delta.
- SLOs for onboarding pilot: 99.5% of cohort B requests must meet p50 latency <= 120ms; 99% for p95 <= 400ms.

Rollout plan and milestones
- Week 0 (prep): implement tenant metadata + variant-mapping.
- Week 2 (alpha): enable Cohort C for 5 internal customers and run synthetic traffic for 72 hours.
- Week 4 (beta): invite 10 developer customers via self-serve onboarding flow. Monitor credit burn and quality regressions.
- Week 8 (pilot review): analyze cohort-level economics, surface pitch for formal pricing adjustments.
- Week 12 (expand): enable automated graduation rules and add cohort-aware default in Console templates.

KPIs and success criteria
- Onboarding-to-paid conversion rate >= 18% within 60 days (target for pilot customers).
- Average cost per 1k tokens for converted customers not > 25% of projections for Cohort B baseline.
- Shadow-eval regression alert rate < 1% for promoted tenants.

Rollback and incident playbook
1) Detection: regression alert triggers on-call, CSM informed.
2) Immediate action: flip tenant to prior fidelity_tag, revoke promotion, and issue one-time debugging credits.
3) Postmortem: include shadow-eval logs, sample prompts, token-level traces, and time-series of latency and burn rate.

Billing and finance checklist
- Finance must approve the credit-expense budget for the pilot and receive weekly burn rate updates.
- Define an accounting tag for onboarding credits to separate promotional cost center.

Console UX notes (developer-facing)
- Onboarding banner in Console with cohort, credits remaining, expected upgrade path, and a one-click request to speak with SE (optional).
- Visual timeline showing days until automatic promotion or expiry.

Sample API mapping snippet (tenant metadata update)
{ "tenant_id": "acct_12345", "onboarding_cohort": "cohort_b", "onboarding_credits": 2500, "onboarding_expires_at": "2028-09-02T00:00:00Z" }

Appendix: example console dashboard panels to build
1) Cohort distribution heatmap by tenant size and industry.
2) Credit velocity timeseries (daily & hourly) with anomaly detection.
3) Shadow-eval regression table with sample failing prompts and links to recordings.

Open questions and recommended experiments
- Should promotions be rate-limited to avoid capacity spikes? Recommendation: stagger promotions by rolling window (max 5% of tenants per hour).
- What is the optimal trial credit sizing per industry? Recommendation: run a 3-month A/B test with stratified sampling by ARR and expected daily tokens.
